questions.question: Which Balkan country is Europe's youngest nation, gaining independence in 2008?
questions.funFact: Kosovo is Europe's youngest country, declaring independence in 2008!
questions.didYouKnow: The town of Prizren hosts one of the oldest medieval festivals in the Balkans.

questions.question: Where was the necktie (cravat) invented?
questions.funFact: The necktie (cravat) originated in Croatia - Croatian soldiers wore them in the 17th century!
questions.didYouKnow: Game of Thrones filmed many scenes in Dubrovnik, known as the Pearl of the Adriatic.

questions.question: Which country is the world's leading producer of rose oil?
questions.funFact: Bulgaria is the world's leading producer of rose oil, used in perfumes worldwide!
questions.didYouKnow: Bulgarians shake their heads for yes and nod for no - opposite to most countries.

questions.question: Which country is known as the birthplace of democracy and the Olympics?
questions.funFact: Ancient Greece gave us democracy, the Olympics, philosophy, and many scientific principles.
questions.didYouKnow: Greece has over 6000 islands, though only about 227 are inhabited.

questions.question: Which landlocked Balkan country borders Greece, Bulgaria, Serbia, Kosovo, and Albania?
questions.funFact: Lake Ohrid is one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes, over 3 million years old.
questions.didYouKnow: North Macedonia is home to Stobi, a famous Roman archaeological site.

questions.question: Which country was part of Yugoslavia until 2006?
questions.funFact: Belgrade has been destroyed and rebuilt 44 times throughout history.
questions.didYouKnow: Serbia produces about 30% of the world's raspberries.

questions.question: Which country became independent from the Ottoman Empire in 1912?
questions.funFact: Albania has over 750000 bunkers built during the communist era.
questions.didYouKnow: The Albanian Riviera has some of Europe's most beautiful beaches.

questions.question: Which country championed the UN's creation of World Bee Day due to its strong beekeeping tradition?
questions.funFact: Slovenia has over 28000 winemakers for a population of only 2 million.
questions.didYouKnow: Postojna Cave is one of the world's largest karst cave systems.

questions.question: Which country's name literally means 'Black Mountain'?
questions.funFact: Montenegro means Black Mountain and the country has dramatic mountain landscapes.
questions.didYouKnow: The Bay of Kotor is often called Europe's southernmost fjord.

questions.question: Which Balkan country has three main ethnic groups: Bosniaks, Serbs, and Croats?
questions.funFact: The Stari Most bridge in Mostar is a UNESCO heritage site rebuilt after war destruction.
questions.didYouKnow: Bosnian coffee culture is a social ritual that can last for hours.
